data.name: Sprocket.Pick.TagPending
data.comment: Tag under a member in the picker's column of what can be done to the chosen blocks, for a member that is not offered yet.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.TagUnsupported
data.comment: Tag under a member in the picker's column of what can be done to the chosen blocks, for a member that cannot be offered.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Power
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about running and electricity, such as a block's power switch, a battery's charge mode and stored power, and the output of reactors, solar panels and wind turbines.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Movement
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values that move a joint or wheel, such as a rotor's or hinge's speed, limits and rotate-to angle, a piston's extend, retract and position, and a wheel's steering angle.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Opening
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values for opening and closing, such as a door's or hangar door's open switch.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Locking
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values for holding fast to something else, such as a landing gear's or connector's lock and status, a connector's docked ship, a merge block's status and a rotor's lock.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Flight
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values for flying the construct, such as a thruster's override and thrust, a gyroscope's override and yaw, pitch and roll, the handbrake, dampeners and autopilot, and a jump drive's jump and distance.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Cargo
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about what a block holds, such as inventory fill and mass, an assembler's or refinery's input and output fill, a connector's collect-all and throw-out, and a sorter's drain-all and filter list.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Air
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about the air in a room, such as an air vent's depressurize switch, room status, oxygen level and flow, and a cryo chamber's air.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Gas
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about gas held or made, such as a tank's stockpile switch and fill level, an O2/H2 generator's gas, and an oxygen farm's output.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Fuel
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about what an engine burns, such as a hydrogen engine's hydrogen level and its running out of hydrogen.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.LifeSupport
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about the air kept for whoever sits or sleeps in a block, such as a cockpit's or a cryo chamber's oxygen level.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Repair
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about how whole a block is and the parts it is built from, such as integrity, damaged, build level, a rotor's add head and a suspension's wheel attached.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.State
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about how a block and its construct stand, counted and weighed, such as an upgrade module's connections and upgrade count and a cockpit's ship mass.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Usage
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about who is using a block now, such as a cockpit's occupant name and under control, a turret controlled by a person and a camera in use.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Production
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about making things, such as an assembler's or refinery's queue, progress and repeat mode, a projector's projecting and blocks left, and a drill's mode.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Weapons
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values for shooting, such as shoot and shoot once, a warhead's detonate and countdown, ammo type and reload, a turret's targeting reset and targeting groups.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Detection
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values for watching for something, such as a sensor's field sides (left, right, top, bottom, front, back) and an event controller's condition and threshold.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Automation
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values that set something else going, such as a timer block's start, stop, trigger and delay, a programmable block's run, and an AI block's mission, follow and path recording.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Behavior
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about how a block behaves on its own or was tuned when built, such as a landing gear's autolock, show on HUD, a sensor's detect switches, ranges, speed limits, torque and an AI block's targets.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Signals
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values for talking to other constructs and to people, such as a broadcast controller's messages, an antenna's broadcast switches, a laser antenna's GPS target, and an action relay's channel and send signal.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Appearance
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about how a block looks, such as a light's color, radius, intensity, falloff and blink interval.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Screens
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about what a block writes on itself, such as a text panel's text, font, font size, colors and alignment, a button panel's labels, an emotion controller's face and a store's shown item.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Sound
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about noise, such as a sound block's play, stop, volume, range and loop length.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Identity
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about what a block is called, such as its name, HUD text and a button's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Access
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values about who may use a block, such as anyone-can-use, ownership, faction, a spawn point's name and a safe zone's permission switches.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Other
data.comment: A heading in the picker's organized list of what the chosen blocks offer, over the actions and values that belong under no other heading or that nobody has placed, such as a block's custom data. It is always the last heading.

data.name: Sprocket.Rate.EveryTickCost
data.value: Sixty times a second is costly; worth it only where nothing slower will do.
data.comment: Caution in the length panel for how often an Every trigger runs, shown while the length is one tick.

data.name: Sprocket.Rate.FastCost
data.value: Six times a second is still costly; try something slower first.
data.comment: Caution in the length panel for how often an Every trigger runs, shown while the length is two to ten ticks.

data.name: Sprocket.Wait.InSeconds
data.comment: In the length panel (opened by pressing a wait step's length on a sequence's screen or a timer trigger's rate on a logic system's screen, and part of the picker for a timer trigger): the option beside the number that gives the length in seconds; also beside the number of a length an action takes, among its options in the picker.

data.name: Sprocket.Wait.InTicks
data.comment: In the length panel (opened by pressing a wait step's length on a sequence's screen or a timer trigger's rate on a logic system's screen, and part of the picker for a timer trigger): the option beside the number that gives the length in ticks; also beside the number of a length an action takes, among its options in the picker.

data.name: Sprocket.Wait.PickSeconds
data.comment: In the length panel (opened by pressing a wait step's length on a sequence's screen or a timer trigger's rate on a logic system's screen, and part of the picker for a timer trigger): a button in the row of ready lengths, shown while the length is given in seconds; {count} is the number of seconds (0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10 or 30).

data.name: Sprocket.Wait.PickMinute
data.comment: In the length panel (opened by pressing a wait step's length on a sequence's screen or a timer trigger's rate on a logic system's screen, and part of the picker for a timer trigger): the button in the row of ready lengths that gives 60 seconds, shown while the length is given in seconds.

data.name: Sprocket.Wait.PickTicks
data.comment: In the length panel (opened by pressing a wait step's length on a sequence's screen or a timer trigger's rate on a logic system's screen, and part of the picker for a timer trigger): a button in the row of ready lengths, shown while the length is given in ticks; {count} is the number of ticks (1, 10, 30, 60, 100 or 300).

data.name: Sprocket.Time.JustNow
data.comment: When a sequence last ran, shown on the sequence's row on a logic system's screen and in the status line at the top of the sequence's own screen, for the first two seconds after it ran.

data.name: Sprocket.Time.UnderMinute
data.comment: When a sequence last ran, shown on the sequence's row on a logic system's screen and in the status line at the top of the sequence's own screen, from two seconds until a minute after it ran.

data.name: Sprocket.Time.MinuteAgo
data.comment: When a sequence last ran, shown on the sequence's row on a logic system's screen and in the status line at the top of the sequence's own screen, between one and two minutes after it ran.

data.name: Sprocket.Time.MinutesAgo
data.comment: When a sequence last ran, shown on the sequence's row on a logic system's screen and in the status line at the top of the sequence's own screen, from two minutes until an hour after it ran. {count} is the whole number of minutes, 2 to 59.

data.name: Sprocket.Time.HourAgo
data.comment: When a sequence last ran, shown on the sequence's row on a logic system's screen and in the status line at the top of the sequence's own screen, once an hour or more has passed since it ran.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.AtLeast
data.comment: In the picker's values column, after a value's name beside its box, when the value has only a lower limit. {least} is that limit.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.AtMost
data.comment: In the picker's values column, after a value's name beside its box, when the value has only an upper limit. {most} is that limit.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.Either
data.comment: The words a word value can be, listed beside its box in the picker's values column and in the refusal under that column. {rest} is every word but the last, separated by commas; {last} is the last word.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.Needed
data.comment: Refusal under the picker's values column when a value that is needed is empty, or when no value at all is filled in. {name} is the value's name, starting with a capital, or its number in the order for a value without one.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.OneOf
data.comment: Refusal under the picker's values column when a word value is not one of the words it can be. {name} is the value's name; {words} is the list of words it can be, the last joined by "or".

data.name: Sprocket.Value.Number
data.comment: Refusal under the picker's values column when a value that must be a number is not. {name} is the value's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.Whole
data.comment: Refusal under the picker's values column when a value that must be a whole number has a fraction. {name} is the value's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.Within
data.comment: Refusal under the picker's values column when a number is outside its limits. {name} is the value's name; {range} is the limits in words, such as "between 0 and 30".

data.name: Sprocket.Value.AboveAtMost
data.comment: The limits in a refusal under the picker's values column, for a number that must be more than {least} and at most {most}.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.Between
data.comment: The limits in a refusal under the picker's values column, for a number that must be from {least} to {most}, both included.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.Above
data.comment: The limit in a refusal under the picker's values column, for a number that must be more than {least} and has no upper limit.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.OrMore
data.comment: The limit in a refusal under the picker's values column, for a number that must be {least} or more and has no upper limit.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.OrLess
data.comment: The limit in a refusal under the picker's values column, for a number that must be {most} or less and has no lower limit.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.Numbered
data.comment: What a refusal under the picker's values column calls a value that has no name. {number} is its place in the order, counting from 1.

data.name: Sprocket.Setting.Name
data.comment: In the panel New setting... opens from a value's link mark, the label of the box the new setting's name is typed in.

data.name: Sprocket.Setting.Numbered
data.comment: The name a new setting starts with in the panel New setting... opens, numbered after it where the logic system has a slot or setting called so.

data.name: Sprocket.Setting.Default
data.comment: In the panel New setting... opens from a value's link mark, the label of the value an installation that chooses none uses. Left empty, every installation must choose the setting.

data.name: Sprocket.Setting.Holds
data.comment: In the panel a setting is made or opened in, the label of what the setting holds: on or off, a number, text, a length of time or one of the logic system's state types. It can be chosen only while the setting is made from the installation panel, and is shown but not changeable otherwise.

data.name: Sprocket.Setting.DefaultHint
data.value: Leave the default empty, and each installation must set its own.
data.comment: In the panel a setting is made or opened in, under its default, where the default may be left empty.

data.name: Sprocket.Setting.Value
data.comment: Label of the value in the panel an installation's value of a setting is given in, opened from the setting's row on the installation panel.

data.name: Sprocket.Setting.UseDefault
data.comment: Button in the panel an installation's value of a setting is given in: this installation takes the setting's default again. Shown only for a setting that has a default.

data.name: Sprocket.Setting.KindInteger
data.comment: In the list of what a new setting holds, the setting holds a whole number.

data.name: Sprocket.Setting.KindReal
data.comment: In the list of what a new setting holds, the setting holds a number that may have decimals.

data.name: Sprocket.Setting.KindText
data.comment: In the list of what a new setting holds, the setting holds text.

data.name: Sprocket.Setting.KindDuration
data.comment: In the list of what a new setting holds, the setting holds a length of time.

data.name: Sprocket.Setting.NewType
data.comment: Last choice in the list of what a new setting holds, after the logic system's own state types: it makes a new state type for the setting to hold.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.AddSetting
data.comment: On the installation panel tab of a logic system, in the menu of the "+ slot" button under the slots and at the end of each category of slots. It opens the panel that makes a setting.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.Fixed
data.comment: First choice in the menu under a value's link mark in a values panel: the value is the one typed or chosen in its field, the same for every installation.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.NewSetting
data.comment: Last choice in the menu under a value's link mark in a values panel: opens a form making a new setting for the value.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.ByDefault
data.comment: Beside a setting's name where it stands in for a value in a values panel, and beside each setting in the menu under the value's link mark. {value} is the setting's default, as the value's field would show it.

data.name: Sprocket.Value.SourceAbout
data.value: Select a source for this value.
data.comment: Tip on the link mark at the end of a value's row in a values panel, which opens the menu choosing where the value comes from.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.Short
data.comment: Heading of the short name box on a slot's screen, shown only for a slot that expects a signal: the box holds the few words each button and toolbar slot answering the slot shows.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.ShortHint
data.comment: Placeholder in the empty short name box on a signal slot's screen, under the Short name heading.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.Default
data.comment: The name a new logic system is given when it is added from the home screen. {number} is filled with the first number no logic system is using, counting on from the logic systems there are.

data.name: Sprocket.Terminal.Open
data.comment: The button in a programmable block's terminal that opens the automation editor. Also the fallback label of a toolbar slot holding the block's automation action.

data.name: Sprocket.Terminal.OpenAbout
data.comment: The tooltip on the button in a programmable block's terminal that opens the automation editor.

data.name: Sprocket.Terminal.Hero
data.comment: A label in the terminal of the programmable block that keeps the construct's automation, shown only in developer mode.

data.name: Sprocket.Terminal.Action
data.comment: The name of the programmable block's toolbar action as the game lists it when a toolbar slot is assigned.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.Title
data.comment: Name of the Paused screen in the editor's heading bar. The screen opens in place of the home screen while automation is paused because its construct changed hands.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.Why
data.value: {construct} passed from {before} to {now}, so its automation is paused until you resume it.
data.comment: First sentence of the text in the middle of the Paused screen. {construct} is the construct's name; {before} names the players who owned it, and {now} the players who own it now, each a list separated by commas.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.Someone
data.comment: Stands for a player whose name is not known, in place of {before} or {now} in the sentence on the Paused screen that says the construct changed hands.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.Heading
data.comment: Heading in the middle of the Paused screen, under its picture.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.Size
data.comment: Sentence in the middle of the Paused screen saying how much automation is paused, when the construct holds more than one logic system. {count} is how many.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.SizeOne
data.comment: Sentence in the middle of the Paused screen saying how much automation is paused, when the construct holds exactly one logic system.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.LostOne
data.value: One of its blocks is out of its reach.
data.comment: Sentence in the middle of the Paused screen, shown when exactly one block on the construct is one none of its owners may use, so the automation cannot reach it.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.ReturnedOne
data.value: One is back in its reach.
data.comment: Sentence in the middle of the Paused screen, shown when exactly one block the automation could not reach before the construct changed hands can be reached now.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.RemoveOneQuestion
data.comment: Question dialog asked after pressing Remove all on the Paused screen, when the construct holds exactly one logic system. {construct} is the construct's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.Lost
data.value: {count} of its blocks are out of its reach.
data.comment: Sentence in the middle of the Paused screen, shown when several blocks on the construct are ones none of its owners may use, so the automation cannot reach them. {count} is how many.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.Returned
data.comment: Sentence in the middle of the Paused screen, shown when several blocks the automation could not reach before the construct changed hands can be reached now. {count} is how many.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.Resume
data.comment: Button on the Paused screen: starts the automation again as it was and goes to the home screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.Leave
data.comment: Button on the Paused screen: keeps the automation paused and goes to the home screen, where a banner leads back.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.RemoveAll
data.comment: Button on the Paused screen, and the answer in the question dialog it asks: deletes every logic system on the construct. Each can be brought back with undo on the home screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.RemoveQuestion
data.comment: Question dialog asked after pressing Remove all on the Paused screen, when the construct holds more than one logic system. {count} is how many; {construct} is the construct's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.Banner
data.comment: Banner at the top of every screen of the editor except the Paused screen, while automation is left paused after its construct changed hands. {construct} is the construct's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Paused.Review
data.comment: Button on the banner shown while automation is left paused after its construct changed hands: opens the Paused screen again.

data.name: Sprocket.Terminal.Foreign
data.value: Only the owners of {construct}, and those they share with, can open its automation.

data.name: Sprocket.Repair.ScreenOnBlockSlot.Warning
data.value: This step is outdated and now needs a screen slot. Press {slot} to make one.
data.comment: Warning on a step that does something to a screen (shows text, for example) through a slot made to hold blocks rather than screens, as programs written before screen slots existed do; the step still runs. {slot} is the slot's name. Pressing the slot in the step opens the picker, which makes a screen slot of it. Shown under the step's line on a sequence's screen, on the sequence's row on a logic system's screen, and on the logic system's heading on the home screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Repair.ScreenOnBlockSlot.Instead
data.comment: Quieter words after the proposed name of a new screen slot in the picker's heading, where the step's slot holds blocks and another step or trigger uses it for the blocks themselves, so the picker makes a new screen slot for this step and leaves the old one to the others. {slot} is the name of the step's slot.

data.name: Sprocket.Repair.ScreenOnBlockSlot.AheadInPlace
data.value: {slot} holds blocks, but this step uses its screen. Picking the screen makes {slot} a screen slot, for every step that uses it.
data.comment: Question asked as a step is pressed that shows on a screen (shows text, for example) through a slot made to hold blocks, where every step using the slot uses its screen, before the picker opens. {slot} is the slot's name. The slot keeps its name.

data.name: Sprocket.Repair.ScreenOnBlockSlot.AheadSplit
data.value: {slot} holds blocks, but this step uses its screen. Other steps use {slot} for the block itself, so picking the screen gives every step that uses the screen a new screen slot, and {slot} stays for the block.
data.comment: Question asked as a step is pressed that shows on a screen through a slot made to hold blocks, where other steps or triggers use the slot for the block itself (switching it on or off, for example), before the picker opens. {slot} is the slot's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Repair.ScreenOnBlockSlot.Proceed
data.comment: Answer to the question asked before the picker opens on a step that shows on a screen through a slot holding blocks, the one Enter takes: opens the picker.

data.name: Sprocket.Repair.ScreenOnBlockSlot.Cancel
data.comment: Answer to the question asked before the picker opens on a step that shows on a screen through a slot holding blocks: leaves the step as it is.

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.NothingToAwait
data.value: There are no pending tasks to wait for here, because no step above it takes time.
data.comment: Warning on an await (a wait for what is running) when no step since the previous await takes time to finish. Shown under the await's line on a sequence's screen and on the sequence's row on a logic system's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.NothingToAverage
data.value: This step has no blocks to take an average of.
data.comment: Problem when an if step takes the average of a value over a set that holds no blocks, such as an empty slot, so there is no number to compare and the run ended there. Shown under the step's line on a sequence's screen and on the sequence's row on a logic system's screen; on the home screen (under the logic system's row) and at the top of the installation panel it follows the step number, as in "Step 3: ...".

data.name: Sprocket.Stopped.NothingToAverage
data.value: it had no blocks to take an average of.
data.comment: Reason a run stopped: an if step took the average of a value over a set that holds no blocks, such as an empty slot. It completes the sentence saying why Sprocket switched off a logic system (or one of its installations), such as "Stopped at step 3: ...", shown near the top of the logic system's screen, under its row on the home screen and at the top of the installation panel.

data.name: Sprocket.Problem.Aborted
data.comment: Said where an abort step with no message of its own, set to show as a warning, ended a run: under the step's line on a sequence's screen and on the sequence's row on a logic system's screen; on the home screen (under the logic system's row) and at the top of the installation panel it follows the step number, as in "Step 3: ...". An abort with a message says the message instead, as the player wrote it.

data.name: Sprocket.Stopped.Aborted
data.comment: Reason a run stopped: an abort step with no message of its own, set to show as a problem, ended it and switched the installation off. It completes the sentence saying why Sprocket switched off a logic system (or one of its installations), such as "Stopped at step 3: ...", shown near the top of the logic system's screen, under its row on the home screen and at the top of the installation panel. "abort" is the step's word in the script and stays as it is. An abort with a message says the message instead.

data.name: Sprocket.Abort.Message
data.comment: Label over the box in the small panel that opens from an abort step's line on a sequence's screen: the reason the step gives when it ends the sequence, shown on the sequence as written. It may be left empty.

data.name: Sprocket.Abort.Level
data.comment: Label beside the three words "note", "warning" and "problem" in the small panel that opens from an abort step's line on a sequence's screen: how the step's message shows when it ends the sequence. The three words are the step's words in the script and stay English.

data.name: Sprocket.Guide.RichText
data.value:
# Rich text
Rich text is plain text with a few marks typed into it, taken from Markdown, that turn it into headings, lists, tables, and bold or italic words. This page shows each mark, and what it gives.
## Bold, italic and code
`` **bold** *italic* ***both*** `code` ``
**bold** *italic* ***both*** `code`
## Colors
`[Danger]{color=red} [Caution]{color=#E8B323}`
[Danger]{color=red} [Caution]{color=#E8B323}
A color is a name or a hex code: `#rrggbb`, or `#aarrggbb` with its transparency first. The names are black, white, gray, silver, red, maroon, orange, yellow, olive, lime, green, aqua, teal, blue, navy, fuchsia and purple. Anything else is left as written, brackets and all.
## Headings
`# Large` `## Middle` `### Small`
# Large
## Middle
### Small
## Lines and paragraphs
Enter starts a new line, and a blank line between two lines starts a new paragraph.
## Lists
`- Inner door` `- Outer door` `1. Close the inner door` `2. Depressurize the airlock`
- Inner door - Outer door
1. Close the inner door 2. Depressurize the airlock
## Quotes
`> Wear a helmet before cycling out.`
> Wear a helmet before cycling out.
## Dividing lines
`---`
---
## Centered and right
`::: center` `Hangar 2` `:::`
::: center Hangar 2 :::
`::: right` puts the lines between on the right the same way.
## Tables
`| Room | Vents |` `|:--|--:|` `| Airlock | 1 |` `| Hangar | 4 |`
| Room | Vents | |:--|--:| | Airlock | 1 | | Hangar | 4 |
The second line says how each column lines up: `:--` left, `:-:` centered, `--:` right.
To leave out the heading, start the table with a row of empty cells:
`| | |` `|:--|--:|` `| Airlock | 1 |` `| Hangar | 4 |`
| | | |:--|--:| | Airlock | 1 | | Hangar | 4 |
A table is as wide as its cells. Add a star into a column's dashes, as in `:--*`, to stretch the table across the page, that column taking a share of it. Stars set the shares: `|:--*|:--*|` gives two columns half each, while `|:--*|:--***|` gives one column a quarter and the other three quarters. A column without a star keeps the width of its cells, and the starred ones share what is left.
`| Room | Vents |` `|:--*|--:|` `| Airlock | 1 |`
| Room | Vents | |:--*|--:| | Airlock | 1 |
## Writing a mark as itself (escape character)
`\*Inner door\*`
\*Inner door\*
A backslash before a mark shows the mark as it is typed.
## Keeping words together
`10 SC`
10 SC
` ` is a space a line never breaks at, so the words either side of it stay on one line. It keeps a mark with the link after it too: `![](mark:trigger) [triggers](Term.Trigger)`.
## Writing a character by its name or number
`<Inner door> & ©`
<Inner door> & ©
`&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` write &, <, >, " and '. Any character can be written by its number, as `©` or `©` for ©. An `&` that starts none of these is written as it is typed.
data.comment: The guide to formatting text, shown in its own window opened by the Markup button by a description box on a logic system's screen and on a slot's screen. Its first line, starting "# ", is the window's title; the rest shows each mark of rich text and what it gives, so the marks in the examples are kept as they are.
